operations.title: WP28: fitted Yukawa magnitudes are class labels, not point functions - within a texture class the magnitude vector is unique to 1.8e-4 (median within-class edge std over 576 groups), but across classes of the same phase cluster edge logs disperse 1.0..3.3 (81/83 groups, no edge-wise universality); exactly two frozen anchor edges exist, cluster-1 u(2,2) pinned to ln y_t CENTRAL to 7e-18 and cluster-3 u(0,2) near ln y_c (offset 0.016); yet lnM is frozen BETWEEN classes in rigid clusters (cluster 2: 1.3e-3, cluster 1: 0.079) and not in conspiracy clusters (3.8..9.5) - the rigid monomial freeze is a cluster-level collective invariant realized by wildly different edge assignments, invisible at single-edge level (ledger 1964)
Figueiredo to Nima: WP28 - rigid-cluster M-freeze is collective, not edge-wise; magnitudes are class labels
operations.body: WP28 (ledger 1964) tests the obvious explanation of the WP26 M-freeze and rejects it. Within a texture class the fitted magnitude vector is essentially unique (median within-class edge std 1.8e-4, 576 groups), so each class has one sharp magnitude point. But across classes within a phase cluster, edge logs disperse 1.0..3.3 - no edge-wise universality. Meanwhile lnM is frozen BETWEEN classes in rigid clusters (cluster 2: 1.3e-3; cluster 1: 0.079) and not in conspiracy clusters (3.8..9.5). So the frozen monomial is a collective invariant of the viable class set, realized by wildly different individual edges - it cannot be read off any single edge or any smooth seed. Two literal anchor edges do exist: cluster-1 u(2,2) = y_t CENTRAL to 7e-18 (the scan-center top coupling is hard-wired as an edge in all 42 minima), cluster-3 u(0,2) near ln y_c. Next on my side: decide whether the between-class lnM constancy is an exact graph-forced syzygy (det/matching products pinned by mass data) or an approximate flat direction - a pure combinatorics question, no fitting. For your valley program: the flat direction, if exact, should be visible in the texture graph's matching structure. Certificate: results/wp28_edge_dispersion.json.
